extracted.intended_audience: writers, dramatists, and critics of comedy; literary students and theatre practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating and evaluating 'pure Comedy' (stage/novel/poem) that emphasizes the Comic idea, character-types, tone, and social conditions rather than elaborate plotting. Focuses on cultivating comic perception and differentiating comic effects from satire, irony, and humour.

rubrics_metrics.name: The life of the comedy is in the idea
rubrics_metrics.description: The life of the comedy is in the idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plots may be thin; the compelling element is a commanding Comic idea that animates character and scene. Example: 'The fable is thin... The life of the comedy is in the idea.' Anti-pattern: substituting elaborate contrivance for a guiding Comic conception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character realism combined with idealization
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters should be realistic in painting yet also idealized in the way they embody types or ideas ('Menander and Moliere stand alone specially as comic poets of the feelings and the idea').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce figures that feel 'real' in motive and detail (e.g., Celimene's mind in movement) but who also express broader comic types (e.g., Alceste as the satirist). Too literal realism without the idea weakens Comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active vs passive comic roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish active comic spirits (who drive the comedy) from passive comic figures: 'Celimene is the active spirit... Alceste is only passively comic.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure at least one character actively animates the comic situation; passive characters can be comic through their reactions but should not be the sole engine of the piece.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comic requires knowledge of the real world and human nature
rubrics_metrics.description: To love Comedy you must know the real world, and know men and women well enough not to expect too much of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comic perception depends on accurate social observation—recognize follies, classes, and conventions so the Comic idea can play against them. Anti-pattern: broad abstract theorizing detached from observed social behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy presupposes some social equality and public life
rubrics_metrics.description: There never will be civilization where Comedy is not possible; and that comes of some degree of social equality of the sexes. 'Where the veil is over women's-faces, you cannot have society... where women are household drudges, the form of Comedy is primitive.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the social conditions in the work allow for conversational, social interplay—Comedy flourishes where both sexes have voice and public presence. Settings that suppress social interchange tend toward primitive or sentimental drama.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Comic idea combats Folly early and perceptively
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comic, or the Comic element, is the specific for the poison of delusion while Folly is passing from vapour to substantial form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comedy to expose follies promptly and sharply rather than allowing them to ossify; the Comic is vigilant and moves quickly against absurdities. Anti-pattern: defensive, plodding responses that give Folly time to entrench.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid contempt and anger in comic perception
rubrics_metrics.description: Contempt is a sentiment that cannot be entertained by comic intelligence... If we do not feign when we say that we despise Folly, we shut the brain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comic tone should perceive and expose without descending into disdain or wrath. Anger and disdain are signs of failure of comic perception and slip into satire or moral scolding rather than Comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish Comic from Satire, Irony, and Humour
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comic is not to be confounded with satire (which sharply drives into sensibilities), irony (stinging under a semi-caress), or humour (which comforts and pities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose your dominant mode deliberately: Comedy should balance exposure and sympathy differently from satire (severity), irony (ambiguity of hurt), and humour (comfort/pity). Examples: satire stings; irony ambushes; humour pities while Comedy 'enfolds' these powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address the wits for laughter (not mere jokers)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comic differs from jokers in addressing the wits for laughter; jokers shoot gags for popular sentiment but do not cultivate the Comic idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim comic effects at perceptive readers/listeners who can appreciate subtlety and the Comic idea rather than relying on low or broad joke machinery. Anti-pattern: overreliance on punning and humouristic phrase that blunts perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of types and inherited comic characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Great comic poets have given principal types to Comedy (e.g., Tartuffe = hypocrite; Orgon = dupe; Alceste = 'Manly' misanthrope; Sganarelle, Arnolphe, Figaro, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ and adapt established comic archetypes—they give instant recognizability and can be freshened by the Comic idea. Guidance: idealize upon life to paint types with spiritual strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate 'common-sense' as a comic basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The basis of the Comic is an esteem for common-sense. Comedy is the vigilant first-born of common-sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground comic judgments in everyday rational sensibility; ridicule absurd departures from common-sense rather than merely the odd or grotesque. Anti-pattern: celebrating obscurity or contrived cleverness divorced from common-sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone: blend exposure with pity and shared humanity
rubrics_metrics.description: If you laugh all round him, tumble him, roll him about, deal him a smack, and drop a tear on him... it is a spirit of Humour that is moving you. The Comic enfolds a thinner form of these powers, differing from satire in not sharply driving into the quivering sensibilities, and from humour in not comforting them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for a tone that exposes foibles while retaining sympathy—avoid cruel derision. Example: Fielding's mixture of comic and humorous corrective methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Comic requires receptive readers/viewers
rubrics_metrics.description: You must love pure Comedy warmly to understand the Misanthrope: you must be receptive of the idea of Comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that audience disposition matters: comedic effects rely on an audience trained to perceive the Comic; cultivation (education, taste) enhances reception. Implication for writers: craft with an intended perceptive audience in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lightness and rapid perception over heavy moralizing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comic is a vigilant, quick spirit, never fretting, never tiring, sure of having Folly, allowing her no rest. Our modern system of combating her is too long defensive, and carried on too ploddingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer nimble comic devices that expose absurdity swiftly rather than lumbering moral arguments. Anti-pattern: slow, heavy-handed polemics that deaden comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy can perform political critique via laughter
rubrics_metrics.description: Aristophanes used laughter as a political weapon to attack sophists, demagogues, and public absurdities; political Comedy can make public affairs 'spin along more briskly.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When engaging public themes, use comic devices to reveal folly in politics—be aware of limits (historical censorship/fines) but recognize the power of satirical-laughter blended with comic perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid punning and excessive humouristic phrase
rubrics_metrics.description: The sense of the Comic is much blunted by habits of punning and of using humouristic phrase... it really may be humorous, of a kind, yet it will miss the point by going too much round about it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist cheap verbal tricks that substitute for a sustained Comic idea; prioritize direct perceptive depiction over glib wordplay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the audience share Orgon's comic sympathy to accept ludicrous premises
rubrics_metrics.description: To have killed it too wrathfully!... After this masterstroke of the Comic, you not only put faith in Orgon's roseate prepossession, you share it with him by comic sympathy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build small, credible comic touches that win audience sympathy for a character's mistaken view so the larger comic irony/situation can land. Technique: use vivid, humanizing detail to enlist the audience before turning the joke.
